rated_messages.input_message: If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, try taking the next call in a place where you can't smoke and focus on the conversation. The urge will pass.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.

Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
This craving is just an event. A game. It will pass. The game gets easier the more you let your urge pass without smoking. But, it gets harder every time you give in to the urge and smoke.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
Life can get you really stressed out, but turning to cigs isn't the answer. Call or text family and friends instead. Ask them to help you stay on track.
